wikipedia#0.title: 2015: Lam Wing-kee, the owner of Causeway Bay Books in Hong Kong, known for publishing political books banned in mainland China, was abducted by Chinese authorities.

wikipedia#1.title: 2004: English football club Manchester United defeated rivals Arsenal 2–0 in the Battle of the Buffet, ending the latter's record-breaking unbeaten run.

wikipedia#2.title: 2003: The inaugural Afro-Asian Games opened in Hyderabad, with 2,040 athletes from 96 nations competing.

wikipedia#3.title: 1975: In protest against wage discrepancy and unfair employment practices, 90 percent of Iceland's female population went on strike for a day.

wikipedia#4.title: 1972: Three people were killed when falsework collapsed during the construction of the Loddon Bridge in Berkshire, leading to reform of construction practices in the UK.

wikipedia#5.title: 1964: Charges in a military court against generals Dương Văn Đức and Lâm Văn Phát of leading a coup attempt against South Vietnamese leader Nguyễn Khánh, were dropped.

wikipedia#6.title: 1949: The cornerstone of the United Nations headquarters was laid in New York City.

wikipedia#7.title: 1945: The Charter of the United Nations entered into force after being ratified by the five permanent members of the Security Council and a majority of the other signatories.

wikipedia#8.title: 1944: World War II: The Japanese battleship Musashi, one of the heaviest and most powerfully armed ever constructed, was sunk by American aircraft during the Battle of Leyte Gulf.

wikipedia#9.title: 1931: The George Washington Bridge (pictured), connecting Manhattan, New York City, to Fort Lee, New Jersey, and today the world's busiest motor-vehicle bridge, was dedicated.

wikipedia#10.title: 1930: The Pacification Junta deposed Brazillian president Washington Luís, ending the Brazilian Revolution of 1930.

wikipedia#11.title: 1929: On "Black Thursday", the New York Stock Exchange lost 11 percent of its value at the opening bell on very heavy trading, marking the beginning of the Great Depression.

wikipedia#12.title: 1889: Sir Henry Parkes, Premier of the Colony of New South Wales, gave a speech in which he called for the federation of the six Australian colonies.

wikipedia#13.title: 1885: The Russian ship Dmitry ran aground in Whitby, an incident that inspired the arrival of Count Dracula to England in Bram Stoker's 1897 novel (cover pictured).

wikipedia#14.title: 1851: Umbriel and Ariel, the third- and fourth-largest moons of Uranus, were discovered by William Lassell.

wikipedia#15.title: 1796: War of the First Coalition: The Battle of Schliengen was fought between the French and Austrian armies, who both claimed victory.

wikipedia#16.title: 1789: The Brabant Revolution, sometimes considered to be the first expression of Belgian nationalism, began with the invasion of the Austrian Netherlands by an émigré army from the Dutch Republic.

wikipedia#17.title: 1260: Qutuz (bust pictured), the sultan of Egypt, was assassinated and replaced by fellow Mamluk leader Baybars.
